correctness.rationale: At small \(\mu\), substituting \(2\pi-t_g=s u\) with \(s=\sqrt\mu\) removes the double degeneracy and the implicit-function expansion gives \(u=2\sqrt\pi-(2/3)\pi^{3/2}s^2+O(s^3)\); exponentiation yields the stated \(H_g\) and width. At large \(\mu\), the left side of the grazing equation vanishes at \(t_0=\pi+\arctan(1/\mu)\), and the exact trigonometric rewrite shows the true root differs by only \(O(e^{-\pi\mu}/\mu)\). Expanding \(t_0\), \(H_g\), and \((2\cosh(\pi\mu)-1)^{-1}\) gives the displayed coefficients. Independent numerical root checks converge to the predicted small- and large-parameter rescalings.

final_claim: The oscillatory wedge of arXiv:2609.33034 has two sharply different endpoint scales: as \(\mu\to0^+\), \(t_g=2\pi-2\sqrt\pi\,\mu^{1/2}+O(\mu^{3/2})\) and \(H_{crit}-H_g=4\pi\mu-4\sqrt\pi\,\mu^{3/2}+O(\mu^2)\); as \(\mu\to\infty\), \(H_{crit}=e^{-\pi\mu}+e^{-2\pi\mu}+O(e^{-3\pi\mu})\) while \(H_g=e^{-2}e^{-2\pi\mu}(1+2/(3\mu^2)+O(\mu^{-4}+e^{-\pi\mu}))\).
limitations: The expansions concern the exact symmetric zero-divergence normal form and its simple-period wedge.
